verdict.rationale: PostHog's feature-flag docs cover all three targeting dimensions the story names: rolling a flagged change out to a percentage of users ("1% of users"), and targeting by person property or cohort, with instant turn-off and no redeploy. The Slack agent example of rolling out to users with a given email property reinforces property-based targeting. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of flag targeting, and deeper first-party detail on combining conditions and how percentage rollouts are kept consistent per user.

support.subject: As a developer, I can roll out features behind flags targeted by user properties, cohorts, and percentage rollouts

citations.quote: Wrap a change in a flag, roll it out to 1% of users, watch what happens, and turn it off the moment something looks wrong – no redeploy, no hotfix.
Roll out by person property, cohort, or group, then see the session replays, events, and exceptions from the people who got the flag
@PostHog add a feature flag to the new checkout page and roll it out to everyone with an @example.com email address
